title: Node.js October 21, 2026 security release
unpatched_lines_note: Every release line without an entry in `fixed` (20 and older, and odd-numbered non-LTS lines such as 23 and 25) is end-of-life, still affected, and gets no fix. Upgrade to 22, 24 or 26.

cves.summary: Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write permits remote code execution
dns.resolve truncates names containing a NUL character
TLS certificate hostname bypass when the IP is written in fullwidth digits
TLS certificate hostname bypass when the host loosely resolves to an IP address
Keep-alive socket processes a response written before the request was sent
Non-canonical IPv4 hostnames let DNS SANs authenticate IP endpoints
crypto.randomUUID()/randomInt() entropy caches saved into startup snapshots and SEAs
ZipFile returns attacker-controlled prefix bytes after failed header validation
Permission Model filesystem over-grant via wildcard radix lookup

notes: Bundled dependency updates: c-ares (22/24/26), CA certificates with the eMudhra intermediate CA removed (22/24/26), OpenSSL (22/24), SQLite (22), Undici (22/24/26). Test outbound TLS after upgrading.
Prioritize internet-facing services that decompress Brotli (HTTP clients, servers, proxies, zlib.createBrotliDecompress) and TLS clients that connect to user-supplied hosts.
Electron apps, vendor images and appliances bundle their own Node.js; flag them for a vendor update instead of patching in place.
